source: built-in alcohol_cvd example; linear, two-stage, REML, Greenland–Longnecker
plain: This analysis combined 6 studies with 19 non-reference dose levels to estimate how relative risk varies with dose. k = 6 studies, 19 non-reference doses · linear trend · two-stage, REML, Greenland–Longnecker covariance Pooled slope −0.004365 log RR per unit of dose (SE 0.00589); RR per unit = 0.9956 [0.9842, 1.0072]. For the linear trend there is no clear evidence of a difference (the confidence interval includes no effect). Variation beyond chance may represent substantial heterogeneity (I² = 64.7%). The shaded band describes uncertainty in the average curve, not the range of effects in a new study. These associations do not establish causation or clinical importance.
methods: Dose-response meta-analysis used a linear trend on the log relative risk scale. The two-stage approach fitted study coefficients by generalised least squares, then pooled the coefficient vectors. Pooling used restricted maximum likelihood. Within-study covariance used Greenland–Longnecker reconstruction. The supplied study design, counts, log relative risks and standard errors were retained; reference rows have blank standard errors. Dose bases were centred at each study’s reference for fitting and at the chosen reference for prediction. Coefficient tests used normal z statistics, and joint dose tests used Wald chi-squared statistics. The 95% coefficient and curve confidence intervals used the normal quantile times the standard error; curve variance was the centred design vector times the coefficient covariance matrix times its transpose. Log relative risks and their confidence limits were exponentiated to report relative risks. No Hartung–Knapp adjustment or prediction interval was computed. Heterogeneity Q used fixed-effect GLS of the study coefficients; I² was the non-negative part of the excess of Q over its degrees of freedom divided by Q, expressed as a percentage. Goodness-of-fit deviance and coefficients of determination used the fixed-effect fit to all non-reference points. Analyses were run in allmeta dose-response-ma <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
results: k = 6 studies, 19 non-reference doses · linear trend · two-stage, REML, Greenland–Longnecker covariance Pooled slope −0.004365 log RR per unit of dose (SE 0.00589); RR per unit = 0.9956 [0.9842, 1.0072]. Coefficients (log relative risk): Term: dose; estimate: −0.0043654; SE: 0.005889; z: −0.74; p: 0.4585; confidence interval: −0.01591 to 0.007177. Heterogeneity, tests and fit: Q test of heterogeneity (all coefficients); Q = 14.146, df = 5, p = 0.0147. I² (from Q); 64.7%. Between-study variance τ²; 1.006e−4 (τ = 0.01003). Wald test, all dose coefficients = 0; χ² = 0.549, df = 1, p = 0.4585. Goodness of fit: deviance (fixed-effect fit to all points); D = 44.527, df = 18, p = 0.0005. Coefficient of determination R² (adjusted); 0.0483 (−0.0045). Log-likelihood (restricted) · AIC; 14.0342 · −24.068. Predicted relative risks: Dose: 0 (reference); RR: 1; confidence interval: —; log RR: 0; SE: —. Dose: 5.04; RR: 0.978; confidence interval: 0.923 to 1.037; log RR: −0.022; SE: 0.0297. Dose: 8.17; RR: 0.965; confidence interval: 0.878 to 1.060; log RR: −0.03567; SE: 0.0481. Dose: 18; RR: 0.924; confidence interval: 0.751 to 1.138; log RR: −0.07858; SE: 0.106. Dose: 29.4; RR: 0.880; confidence interval: 0.626 to 1.235; log RR: −0.1283; SE: 0.173. Dose: 50.1; RR: 0.804; confidence interval: 0.451 to 1.433; log RR: −0.2187; SE: 0.295.
flags: Tests for small-study effects would be underpowered; none were performed.
No prediction interval is available from this app. Confidence intervals describe the mean curve.
